domains.title: Memory, storage and lifetime failure laboratory

objectives.text: Predict which declared detector or invariant monitor can observe an extent, initialization, lifetime or resource defect on a selected path.
Run isolated learner-owned negative and repaired controls with exact build/tool settings and classify observed versus unavailable evidence.
Explain why undefined behavior, native crash details and a clean dynamic report cannot be fixed portable success or failure oracles.

subtopics.title: Object extents, underflow, off-by-one and NUL boundaries

objectives.text: Specify and implement byte-range and string contracts separating capacity, initialized length, signed input index and NUL space.
Locate the first invalid access in lower-bound, upper-bound, one-past and missing-terminator traces before pointer arithmetic or publication.
Repair the contract and verify unchanged outputs on rejection, exact-capacity behavior and a legal-address logical corruption counterexample.

subtopics.title: Checked allocation sizes and integer conversions

objectives.text: Check count, stride, header and terminator arithmetic against the declared representable size limit before each operation.
Distinguish unsigned wrapping, signed undefined overflow and narrowing from an application size-contract violation.
Verify successful boundary allocation and rejection paths with no allocation, mutation or lost ownership on size failure.

subtopics.title: Stack exhaustion, frames and nested execution

objectives.text: Compute a conditional whole-path stack budget from pinned per-function qualifiers, bounded recursion, reentrancy and permitted exception nesting.
Compare that budget with changed-pattern high water and an isolated native exhaustion observation without treating samples as a universal bound.
Distinguish stack-capacity exhaustion from local-buffer corruption and repair depth or frame use while retaining explicit ABI and unknown-frame limits.

subtopics.title: Fixed RAM sections, startup and collision failures

objectives.text: Classify fixed .bss link-region overflow, wrong startup ranges, declared heap/stack collision and stray-write corruption by their distinct first violated invariants.
Derive load/run intervals, aligned fixed section placement and reserved dynamic-region capacity from a supplied synthetic map.
Repair one layout/startup/allocator boundary and verify unchanged retained storage, no overlap and precise link-versus-runtime evidence.

subtopics.title: Leaks, retained storage and failure cleanup

objectives.text: Track each resource acquisition, owning handle, borrowed edge and release across success and every partial-failure prefix.
Distinguish forgotten release, lost owner, indirect lost children and reachable retained storage using a declared finite graph and a separate native leak observation.
Repair cleanup or retention policy and demonstrate exactly-once release, preserved first cause and bounded live and retained byte ledgers.

subtopics.title: Resize, invalid release and stale aliases

objectives.text: Preserve old ownership on failed nonzero resize and invalidate all prior aliases after successful resize even if an address token is reused.
Diagnose double release, interior or foreign release, use-after-free and escaped aliases using a generation/extent history without using invalid C pointers.
Repair ownership and alias publication, test forced failure/movement/address reuse, and explain why free(NULL) or clearing one owner does not repair other aliases.

subtopics.title: Initialization state and delayed invalid use

objectives.text: Separate initialized-field or byte state from addressability, storage acquisition and zero-byte representation assumptions.
Trace the first consumed uninitialized field through propagation to a branch or output and compare supported Memcheck with declared optional MemorySanitizer coverage.
Repair complete initialization and publication, then test different fill patterns, partial failure and field-wise equality without treating padding as semantic state.
Trace buffer and callback-context ownership through submission, timeout, cancellation request, confirmed completion and reuse.
Reject early reclamation, duplicate or stale completions and reentrant scratch-buffer conflicts under an explicit bounded event contract.
Verify repaired ownership in host histories and separately identify target reachability, ordering, interrupt and device-quiescence evidence required for a physical claim.
Build a competing-hypothesis dossier connecting the first invalid state to delayed crash or corrupt-output symptoms.
Select bounded watchpoint, allocation history, map or fault evidence and state timing, scope and frame-validity limits.
Repair the violated invariant, distinguish mitigation from prevention, and pass unseen capacity, failure, nesting and delayed-completion transfer cases.
